newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: A lack of follow-through demand forced long bonds to give up their initial gains and trade little changed from their overnight levels in late Wednesday trade.
At 1400 GMT, the key R150 gilt was pegged at a 14.65 percent yield, unchanged from late Tuesday.
In the morning session, the yield moved to 14.57 percent -- its lowest level since March 13 -- after receiving a fresh fillip from latest government financing figures.

Government raised 3.22 billion rand in the bond markets last month, bringing total financing in the first two months of this fiscal year to 5.88 billion rand -- 22 percent of the total 27 billion rand it plans to raise in the capital market this year.

The data, which was lumped together with other recent bullish data, prompted local institutions, offshore players and jobbers to pile into the market, extending the market's downhill run to over 30 points so far this week.
But at its lows, dealers said the buying fizzled out and the market spent the rest of the day on a retracement path.
"We opened up quite nicely and unfortunately it just collapsed. There was no follow through at all and the market retraced all the way to test its previous break," a senior trader said.

"I got the impression that the guys were a little bit on the long side. They have used a lot of stock to pull the market down to these levels and there hasn't been the follow-through they expected so we might just hang about here for a little while," he said.
A move back up to the 14.68 level was likely in the short-term as the market hunted for fresh buyers, the trader added.

Dealers said that technically the market remained bullish, having broken a number of key levels on the way down this week. They pegged the next target on the downside at around 14.58 to 14.55 percent, a break below which could herald a substantial bull run.
